issues.legal_issue: A will made by a competent and apparently free testator is not invalid for undue influence unless the challenger proves pressure that overbore the testator’s free agency.
material_facts: The testator’s execution of the will and testamentary capacity were undisputed.
The testator had a longstanding grievance about his younger son’s marriage, and the will’s recitals reflected that grievance.
The beneficiary had no part in preparing, executing, or registering the will; the testator made the arrangements himself and kept the will.
The evidence showed that the beneficiary had expressed views to the testator, but did not show that he impaired the testator’s free exercise of volition.
The testator lived for nearly a year after making the will and continued to say that it should stand.
issues.conclusion: The challenger did not prove undue influence, and the will was not invalid on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Under Boyse v. Rossborough and Craig v. Lamoureux, once due execution by a competent person who was apparently a free agent is proved, the burden of proving undue influence rests on the person alleging it. Section 61 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 makes a will void when its making is caused by fraud, coercion, or importunity that takes away the testator’s free agency; Illustration (vii) confirms that persuasion does not invalidate a will where the testator acts in the free exercise of judgment and volition. As explained in Hall v. Hall, persuasion and appeals to affection or other sentiments are legitimate, but pressure that overbears the testator’s volition without convincing the judgment is undue influence.

rule.if: probate_will_proceeding and undue_influence_challenge and will_executed_with_due_formalities and testator_competent_and_apparently_free_agent and not evidence_of_fraud_coercion_or_overbearing_importunity

predicates.probate_will_proceeding: A party seeks probate of a will and another party challenges it.
predicates.undue_influence_challenge: The challenger alleges that a beneficiary caused the testator to make the will through undue influence.
predicates.will_executed_with_due_formalities: The will was executed with the required formalities.
predicates.testator_competent_and_apparently_free_a: The testator had the capacity to make the will and appeared to act freely.
predicates.evidence_of_fraud_coercion_or_overbearin: Evidence shows that fraud, coercion, or pressure overbore the testator’s free agency.
predicates.will_not_invalid_for_undue_influence: The will is not invalid on the ground of undue influence.

issues.definition: When a will is challenged in a probate proceeding, due execution by a competent and apparently free testator, without evidence of fraud, coercion, or overbearing importunity, leads to the will not being invalid for undue influence.

issues.legal_issue: The absence of an attesting witness’s express testimony that the witness signed in the testator’s presence does not by itself establish that a will was not duly attested.
material_facts: The two attesting witnesses testified that the testator signed the will in their presence and that they attested his signature.
The witnesses did not state in their examination-in-chief that they signed the will in the testator’s presence.
The testator and witnesses had assembled by appointment at one place for execution, and the evidence indicated that execution and attestation took place at one sitting.
The witnesses were not cross-examined on the question of attestation, and the lower courts found the will duly attested after considering the evidence.
issues.conclusion: The lower courts’ factual finding that the will was duly attested was accepted; the omission in the witnesses’ examination-in-chief did not require a finding of invalid attestation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 63 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 requires due attestation of a will. Whether attesting witnesses signed in the testator’s presence is a question of fact to be decided from the evidence and circumstances of the case; it cannot be resolved as a matter of law merely because the witnesses did not expressly say so in examination-in-chief.

predicates.probate_will_proceeding: A party seeks probate of a will and another party challenges it.
predicates.due_attestation_challenged: A party disputes whether the will was duly attested.
predicates.attesting_witnesses_omitted_presence_det: The attesting witnesses did not expressly testify in examination-in-chief that they signed in the testator’s presence.
predicates.surrounding_evidence_supports_signing_in: Other evidence or circumstances support that the attesting witnesses signed while the testator was present.
predicates.due_attestation_may_be_found_from_all_ev: Due attestation may be found after evaluating all the evidence and circumstances.

issues.definition: When due attestation is challenged and the witnesses omit an express statement about the testator’s presence, surrounding evidence supporting that presence permits due attestation to be found from all the evidence.
